chunks: I advise you, O people, to fear Allah,
and to praise Him profusely for His favours to you, His blessings upon you, and His trials with you.
How many favours has He singled you out for, and how often has He rescued you with mercy!
You sinned openly; He kept you covered. You behaved in a way to incur His punishment, but He gave you more time!

key_terms.تَدَارَكَكُمْ: He rescued you / He attended to you

ai.seo_question: What does Nahj al-Balagha say about the relationship between human sin and divine mercy?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) frames taqwa not merely as fear, but as an active state of gratitude for both blessings and trials, emphasizing Allah's patience (imla') despite human readiness for punishment. This reflects the Shia understanding of divine mercy as a proactive covering of faults (satr) rather than just the absence of retribution. The passage underscores the transient nature of worldly life as a testing ground where divine forbearance invites spiritual awakening.

en.sayed-ali-raza: I advise you, O people, to fear Allāh
and to praise Him profusely for His favours to you and His reward for you and His obligations on you.
See how He chose you for favours and dealt with you with mercy.
You sinned openly; He kept you covered. You behaved in a way to incur His punishment, but He gave you more time.
